title: LEBER OPTIC ATROPHY AND DYSTONIA
alt_titles: LEBER HEREDITARY OPTIC NEUROPATHY WITH DYSTONIA
DYSTONIA, FAMILIAL, WITH VISUAL FAILURE AND STRIATAL LUCENCIES

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Leber optic atrophy and dystonia (LDYT) is caused by mutation in one of several mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA)-encoded complex I genes, including MTND6, MTND1, and MTND3; mutations in MTND4 have also been implicated.

checks.claim: Leber optic atrophy and dystonia (LDYT) is caused by mutation in one of several mitochondrial DNA-encoded complex I genes.
checks.evidence_quote: This family has similar clinical characteristics as the previously described families with LHON and dystonia with an ND6 mutation.
checks.explanation: The abstract implicates two complex I genes in LHON with dystonia: ND1 in this family and ND6 in earlier families. It does not make the general claim that LDYT is caused by mutation in one of several mtDNA-encoded complex I genes, and it says nothing about ND3.

checks.claim: Mutation in the MTND6 gene causes Leber optic atrophy and dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: A mitochondrial DNA mutation at nucleotide pair 14459 of the NADH dehydrogenase subunit 6 gene associated with maternally inherited Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and dystonia.
checks.explanation: The paper reports an ND6 mutation in a family with LHON and dystonia. It says the evidence suggests this is the disease-causing mutation.

checks.claim: Mutation in the MTND1 gene causes Leber optic atrophy and dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: The 3697G>A/ND1 mitochondrial DNA mutation causes the LHON and spastic dystonia phenotype in the same family.
checks.explanation: The abstract directly states that the ND1 mutation causes the LHON and spastic dystonia phenotype.

checks.claim: Mutation in the MTND3 gene causes Leber optic atrophy and dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: This is the first description of the ND3 mutation causing LDYT.
checks.explanation: The abstract states directly that an ND3 mutation causes LDYT.

checks.claim: Mutations in the MTND4 gene have also been implicated in Leber optic atrophy and dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: A heteroplasmic A-->G transition at nucleotide position 11696 in the ND4 gene resulted in the substitution of an isoleucine for valine at amino acid position 312.
checks.explanation: The ND4 mutation is reported in the family and linked to the phenotype through the complex I deficiency, so it is 'implicated', but only in one family.

paragraphs.text: Leber optic atrophy and dystonia (LDYT) is a maternally inherited mitochondrial disorder associated with variable combinations of vision loss and progressive generalized dystonia (Wang et al., 2009). Within affected families, some members have optic neuropathy, others have dystonia attributed to striatal degeneration, and some have both (Novotny et al., 1986; De Vries et al., 1996).

checks.claim: Leber optic atrophy and dystonia is a maternally inherited mitochondrial disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and dystonia (LDYT) is a mitochondrial disorder associated with variable combinations of vision loss and progressive generalized dystonia.
checks.explanation: The abstract calls LDYT a mitochondrial disorder and reports affected individuals on the maternal side, but it never says 'maternally inherited'.

checks.claim: Leber optic atrophy and dystonia is associated with variable combinations of vision loss and progressive generalized dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and dystonia (LDYT) is a mitochondrial disorder associated with variable combinations of vision loss and progressive generalized dystonia.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this almost word for word.

checks.claim: Within families affected by Leber optic atrophy and dystonia, some members have optic neuropathy, others have dystonia attributed to striatal degeneration, and some have both.
checks.evidence_quote: 8 members had the neuroretinopathy of Leber's disease; 14 had a progressive, generalized dystonia attributed to striatal degeneration; and 1 had both disorders.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes one kindred with members who have each disorder alone or both. The draft also cites De Vries et al. for this point.

paragraphs.text: In a 5-generation Hispanic family with LHON and/or early-onset dystonia, Jun et al. (1994) amplified buffy coat mtDNA from a severely affected child by PCR and sequenced more than 90% of it. The mtDNA was of the Native American haplogroup D genotype and differed from the Cambridge sequence at 40 nucleotide positions. One variant, a G-to-A transition at nucleotide 14459 in the MTND6 gene, changed a moderately conserved alanine to valine at residue 72 (A72V). The variant was not found in 38 Native American haplogroup D mtDNAs or in 108 Asian, 103 Caucasian, or 99 African mtDNAs. Six maternal relatives in 3 generations harbored the mutation, and 1 female with LHON was heteroplasmic.

paragraphs.text: In a large Dutch family with LHON and hereditary spastic dystonia in whom previously reported LHON mtDNA mutations were absent, De Vries et al. (1996) sequenced the protein-coding mitochondrial genes and identified 2 previously unreported mutations: a heteroplasmic A-to-G transition at nucleotide 11696 in the MTND4 gene, resulting in a val312-to-ile (V312I) substitution, and a homoplasmic T-to-A change at nucleotide 14596 in the MTND6 gene, resulting in an ile26-to-met (I26M) substitution. Severe complex I deficiency in muscle provided a link between these mtDNA mutations and the phenotype.

paragraphs.text: In a Chinese family with 18 LDYT patients, Wang et al. (2009) used resequencing microarray analysis of the entire mitochondrial genome and identified a 10197G-A mutation in the MTND3 gene, resulting in an ala47-to-thr (A47T) substitution at a highly conserved residue, on a haplogroup D4b background. The mutation was homoplasmic in leukocytes of all affected individuals on the maternal side. The authors noted that the same mutation had been described in French and Korean patients with Leigh syndrome.

paragraphs.text: In a large Dutch family with LHON and hereditary spastic dystonia, De Vries et al. (1996) identified a homoplasmic T-to-A change at nucleotide 14596 in the MTND6 gene, resulting in an ile26-to-met (I26M) substitution, together with a heteroplasmic 11696A-G mutation in the MTND4 gene. Muscle biopsy showed severe complex I deficiency.

checks.claim: De Vries et al. (1996) identified a T-to-A change at nucleotide 14596 in the MTND6 gene in a large Dutch family with LHON and hereditary spastic dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: a homoplasmic T-->A transition at nucleotide position 14596 in the ND6 gene

checks.claim: The MTND6 14596T-A mutation in the Dutch family was homoplasmic.
checks.evidence_quote: a homoplasmic T-->A transition at nucleotide position 14596 in the ND6 gene
checks.explanation: The paper describes this mutation as homoplasmic.

checks.claim: The MTND6 14596T-A mutation results in an ile26-to-met (I26M) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: resulted in the substitution of a methionine for the isoleucine at amino acid residue 26.

checks.claim: The MTND6 14596T-A mutation occurred together with a heteroplasmic 11696A-G mutation in the MTND4 gene in the Dutch family.
checks.evidence_quote: A heteroplasmic A-->G transition at nucleotide position 11696 in the ND4 gene
checks.explanation: Both mutations were found in the same family; the ND4 mutation is heteroplasmic.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsy in the Dutch family with the MTND6 14596T-A and MTND4 11696A-G mutations showed severe complex I deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: Biochemical analysis of a muscle biopsy revealed a severe complex I deficiency

paragraphs.text: Spruijt et al. (2007) identified a 3697G-A mutation in the MTND1 gene in a patient with LHON who lacked the 3 primary LHON mutations, in a family with LHON and spastic dystonia. The mutation seemed to be associated with an isolated complex I deficiency; the authors noted that it can also cause MELAS syndrome.

checks.claim: Spruijt et al. (2007) identified a 3697G-A mutation in the MTND1 gene in a patient with LHON who lacked the 3 primary LHON mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: The complete mitochondrial DNA was screened for mutations in a patient with LHON without 1 of these 3 primary mutations.
checks.explanation: The patient lacked the 3 primary mutations, and the screen identified the 3697G>A ND1 mutation.

checks.claim: The patient with the MTND1 3697G-A mutation was from a family with LHON and spastic dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: To report a novel mutation that is associated with Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) within the same family affected by spastic dystonia.
checks.explanation: The abstract places the patient in a family affected by both LHON and spastic dystonia.

checks.claim: The MTND1 3697G-A mutation seemed to be associated with an isolated complex I deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: A pathogenic 3697G>A/ND1 mutation was detected and seemed associated with an isolated complex I deficiency.

checks.claim: Spruijt et al. (2007) noted that the MTND1 3697G-A mutation can also cause MELAS syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: This mutation can also cause MELAS syndrome (which encompasses mitochondrial myopathy, encephalopathy, lactic acidosis, and stroke)

paragraphs.text: In a Chinese family with 18 LDYT patients, Wang et al. (2009) identified a 10197G-A mutation in the MTND3 gene, resulting in an ala47-to-thr (A47T) substitution at a highly conserved residue, on a haplogroup D4b background. The mutation was homoplasmic in leukocytes of all affected individuals on the maternal side.

checks.claim: Wang et al. (2009) identified a 10197G-A mutation in the MTND3 gene in a Chinese family with 18 LDYT patients.
checks.evidence_quote: In this paper, we describe a Chinese family with 18 LDYT patients.
checks.explanation: The family and patient count match, and the abstract reports the m.10197G>A mutation in MTND3 in this family.

checks.claim: The MTND3 10197G-A mutation results in an ala47-to-thr (A47T) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: substituting a threonine for a highly conserved alanine at codon 47 of MTND3
checks.explanation: A threonine replacing alanine at codon 47 is A47T.

checks.claim: Residue alanine-47 of MTND3 is highly conserved.
checks.evidence_quote: substituting a threonine for a highly conserved alanine at codon 47 of MTND3
checks.explanation: The abstract describes the alanine at codon 47 as highly conserved.

checks.claim: The MTND3 10197G-A mutation in the Chinese family occurred on a haplogroup D4b background.
checks.evidence_quote: at codon 47 of MTND3 on the background of haplogroup D4b
checks.explanation: The abstract places the mutation on a haplogroup D4b background.

checks.claim: The MTND3 10197G-A mutation was homoplasmic in leukocytes of all affected individuals on the maternal side of the Chinese family.
checks.evidence_quote: Quantitative analysis of the heteroplasmy of the mutation revealed a homoplasmy in the leukocytes of all the affected individuals on the maternal side.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports homoplasmy in leukocytes of all affected maternal-side individuals.

agent.process_note: Read all 8 files in full; all were abstracts only, and Miyoshi et al. (1969) was title only, so it was cited only for its title. No HGNC reference data or gene MIM numbers were supplied, so I left gene MIM numbers and chromosome-location formula details out. Details not found in the abstracts: the protein change for MTND1 3697G-A, heteroplasmy levels in Spruijt et al. (2007), and family sizes and ancestry beyond what the abstracts give. In De Vries et al. (1996) it is unclear which of the 2 mutations (ND4 11696 or ND6 14596) causes the disease, so both were reported as the paper states.
